say.en: A biscuit factory does not sell to every small shop in the country. A wholesaler buys in bulk and supplies the retailers. What does he really add? In this lesson: Distinguish internal and external trade.
Explain the functions and services of wholesalers.
Explain the role of GST in internal trade.

body.en: *Internal* (home) trade is the buying and selling of goods and services within the boundaries of a country; no customs duties are charged and payment is in the national currency. It is of two kinds: wholesale trade (buying in large quantities from producers and selling in smaller lots to retailers or industrial users) and retail trade (selling in small quantities to final consumers). Since July 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) has replaced many indirect taxes, creating a common national market and easing the movement of goods between states.

body.en: *Wholesalers* link many producers with many retailers. They buy in bulk and sell in small lots (breaking bulk), store goods (warehousing), carry stocks so retailers need not, finance producers and retailers, grade and pack goods, transport them, and pass on market information. Eliminating the wholesaler does not eliminate these functions: someone else (the manufacturer or the retailer) must perform them and bear their cost.

say.en: A factory sells a pressure cooker at 1,000 rupees. The wholesaler adds 8 percent and the retailer adds 15 percent. Find the consumer price.
Wholesale price equals 1,000 times 1.08 equals 1,080 rupees.
Retail price equals 1,080 times 1.15 equals 1,242 rupees.
Total margin of middlemen equals 242 rupees.
So the answer is 1,242 rupees.
